content: 1. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This combination is contraindicated and requires close monitoring. 2. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 4. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of pitavastatin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Do not exceed 1 mg/day of pitavastatin. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of serious cardiac effects. 6. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Ponatinib increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of pravastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Risk of toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status. 12. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate, and vice versa, leading to increased toxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity; avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents. 13. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 15. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and promazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of propafenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the effects of protamine by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and quetiapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Monitor closely. 24. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of quinidine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. 26. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and quizartinib both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely with ECG if coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 28. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 29. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Avoid coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters, which may increase systemic exposure to its active metabolite. Coadministration is not recommended. 35. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of rifabutin by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 39. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of rilpivirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of riociguat by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose if needed. 43. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 44. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of rivaroxaban by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially in patients with renal impairment. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of roflumilast by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 50. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor for toxicities. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of seladelpar by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers coadministered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
